correctness.rationale: A five-vertex face contains a unique full block. For a (3,1,1) face deleting a vertex of that block gives a four-vertex face with one possible five-vertex coface, so a unit boundary equation kills the mixed coefficient over Z. Among surviving (3,2) faces each ridge uses exactly its two blocks, so the kernel splits into the top-cycle kernels of the individual six-facet simplex boundaries. Those integral kernels are generated by the alternating boundaries (each ridge equates the two signed facet weights, and the facet adjacency is connected). C5=0. The disjoint facet sets give exactly six facets per nonzero pair coefficient and the vertex support is the union of its active blocks; this proves the sharp minima and the primitive cases. The inclusion retains the old generators and adds r. Swapping two length-three oriented blocks has sign −1 and within-block signs multiply, giving the stated exterior square for the partition-preserving wreath product. This is not a claim that the wreath product exhausts all automorphisms of X2, whose underlying sphere admits S6. The checker was inspected, not rerun; it checks mod-two ranks for r=2–8 and block-permutation symmetry tests for r=2–4 only. Neither test range is used in the integral proof.
residual_risks: No independent checker execution; the unit-coefficient argument proves the unrestricted statement without it.

value.rationale: The family extends the standard two-facet extremal tolerance example by admitting all mixed top faces. Showing precisely why those new faces never contribute to a top cycle gives an integral answer richer than a Leray bound or a Betti number: explicit generators, smallest witnesses and equivariant maps under adding a component. These data are usable in comparisons of tolerance complexes without repeating boundary elimination.
residual_risks: Value is in top-degree chain structure, not a full homotopy computation.
